reader_guide: Start with the overall grade, then read REF-01 and the concurrency and error handling dimensions. Those describe the clearest path by which a dictation could remain in Processing without giving the user an outcome. The other targets mainly reduce the cost of changing code that already has substantial safeguards. Each finding names a source file and exact lines; the quoted snippets are the checkable evidence, while the counterfactual explains the possible effect on this phone. A static risk grade means the code shows a plausible exposure, not that the failure happened on the founder’s S26 Ultra. Use the falsifiability field to see what would settle it. The roadmap orders changes by dependency, not by release date. The distribution counts distinct source locations so a finding repeated as a refactor target is counted once. This is a read-only source review: no build, test, device run, or network inspection was performed. Stage 2 setup and model delivery work, the decided earbud hold, and the decision to require polish are not counted as defects.

overall_grade.rationale: This is professional engineering with real debt, not AI slop. The single session owner, process isolation, fail-open polish, guarded insertion, privacy schemas, and unusually specific outcome tests show deliberate design. The most consequential gap is that a live ASR process can stop answering without a session deadline, leaving the user in Processing. The remaining mass now sits chiefly in DictationSessionCoordinator (1,238 lines), AudioCaptureService (1,000), RecordingAccessibilityOverlay (817), DictionaryScreen (770), and AccessibilityInsertionRunner (716); AppShell is 240 lines and DictationSessionService is 259.
overall_grade.confidence_rationale: The ASR control-flow gap and current file sizes are directly visible. Static review cannot establish vendor hang frequency, framework binder latency, battery cost, or actual insertion success on the S26 Ultra. Priority source files and representative tests were sampled, but this was not a line-by-line review of the whole inventory.

dimensions.name: Architecture integrity
dimensions.justification: The Service is a thin Android shell, AppShell holds navigation, and six surfaces command one coordinator. The largest central file is now the 1,238-line coordinator, not either former extraction target. It still owns an audio-file deletion rule that belongs in the audio cleanup adapter. AudioCaptureService is 1,000 lines despite prior route and picture extractions. No second session owner or identity-based feature gate was found in the sampled paths.

dimensions.name: Concurrency discipline
dimensions.justification: Capture events are pushed off the audio read thread; binder callbacks post to main; service scopes are cancelled. One important wait lacks an owner-side deadline: the coordinator issues ASR and then depends on a callback or process disconnection. A native load or decode that remains alive but never returns produces neither.

best_example.why_exemplary: The audio read thread publishes primitives into a preallocated slot; the worker performs binder delivery.

worst_violation.rule_violated: .claude/rules/architecture-rules.md FACT: heart-and-limbs; named principle: every asynchronous heart request needs a terminal deadline
worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The request starts here; no ASR answer deadline was found in the coordinator, capture controller, or ASR service. Disconnection handles process death but not an alive, stuck process.
worst_violation.counterfactual: After the user stops speaking, the pill can remain in Processing indefinitely and no text or declared error arrives.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: The coordinator advances only through an ASR callback, a thrown request, or a service disconnect after this call.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Hold OfflineRecognizer construction or decode without killing :asr, then demonstrate that the session leaves Processing with one declared failure outcome within a fixed bound.
worst_violation.concurrency_interleaving: 1. The main process enters Processing and queues transcribeFileForTake. 2. The :asr worker enters native model load or decode and never returns, while the process and binder remain alive. 3. No ASR callback or ServiceConnection disconnect occurs. 4. The capture ending has already disarmed its silence bound. 5. The coordinator receives no event that can finish the session.

dimensions.name: Error handling and observability
dimensions.justification: Polish failure paths preserve deterministic text and report a defect; diagnostics generally record shapes instead of dictated content. ASR result delivery is a narrower hole: a callback transaction failure is logged and consumed. The coordinator has no independent ASR deadline to turn that missing result into a user-visible outcome.

best_example.why_exemplary: A failed polish request stops its work and hands the last deterministic text back under a typed reason.

worst_violation.rule_violated: .claude/rules/architecture-rules.md FACT: heart-and-limbs; named principle: terminal delivery failures must reach the request owner
worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The failure is visibly swallowed. Whether a live owner can experience such a callback failure on this phone requires fault injection.
worst_violation.counterfactual: The speech model may have produced words, but the user gets neither those words nor a failure line if callback delivery fails while the owner remains alive.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: The only result delivery is inside runCatching, and its failure branch sends no terminal response.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Inject a callback implementation that throws while the main process remains alive and show one bounded user-visible terminal outcome.
worst_violation.concurrency_interleaving: 1. The :asr worker finishes decoding. 2. Its callback call throws before the main-process listener receives text. 3. The :asr worker logs the class name and returns. 4. The service stays connected, so onSpeechDisconnected does not fire. 5. The main coordinator remains in Processing.

This review did not run them, so it cannot certify that their present environment passes.

dimensions.name: Code hygiene and maintainability
dimensions.justification: Recent splits removed the former AppShell and Service concentration. The next concentration is the 817-line recording overlay, where gesture handling, window placement, appearance, and view construction remain in one type. DictionaryScreen is 770 lines, but its state is already outside the screen in a ViewModel. This is change-risk debt, not evidence of careless generated code.

best_example.why_exemplary: The shell keeps route and presentation state while feature screens and their state owners live elsewhere.

worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The inventory measures 817 lines; this gesture branch and view-building methods later in the same class show the mixed responsibilities.
worst_violation.counterfactual: A visual change to the bubble requires review alongside gesture timing and window behavior, increasing the chance of a touch regression.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: The overlay class owns both gesture transitions and the Android view tree.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Show that the gesture methods and view factory already belong to separate types and the overlay only delegates to them.

dimensions.name: API surface
dimensions.justification: The production capture interface has five methods, parcelables are small, and app-only Kotlin declarations are predominantly internal. Append-only compatibility leaves a legacy byte-array ASR transaction that can exceed Binder's size limit; it is not a current production call, so its user blast radius is low. The old signature must remain declared.

best_example.why_exemplary: The session owner binds a narrow take contract rather than the much larger legacy capture contract.

worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The interface itself documents the limit. The production owner uses the file-path method, and append-only policy prevents deleting the legacy transaction.
worst_violation.counterfactual: An older instrumentation or other internal client using this method for a long recording can fail before ASR receives the request.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: The whole PCM recording is copied into one Binder transaction.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Call the legacy method with a recording above the documented threshold and show the transaction succeeds on the supported phone.

dimensions.name: Performance and latency
dimensions.justification: The capture picture and heartbeat are pushed, and idle publisher work parks without polling. The insertion handoff intentionally waits without a second deadline once its main-thread body starts. That preserves one-write correctness, but the body performs an inline accessibility attempt. Framework response time and any resulting UI stall need a measured device test. The 30-second content-free earbud hold is a decided feature and is not an idle-cost finding.

best_example.why_exemplary: The audio read path avoids a per-frame Binder transaction and wakes a separate publisher only when needed.

worst_violation.rule_violated: .claude/rules/kotlin-patterns.md RULE: never-block-a-binder-or-ui-thread; named principle: bound external waits at an insertion boundary
worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The untimed wait is explicit and intentional. Whether an accessibility action can hold it long enough to affect this phone is a runtime question.
worst_violation.counterfactual: A slow or wedged editor action delays the owner’s insertion handoff and may make the recorder feel stuck after text is ready.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: Once the posted body claims the action, the caller waits for that body's completion without its own deadline.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Use an instrumented editor whose accessibility action is held after the main body claims it; show that the owner still completes handoff and presents a truthful outcome within a measured bound.
worst_violation.concurrency_interleaving: 1. The session worker posts insertion to the accessibility main looper. 2. The main-looper body claims the action. 3. Its inline accessibility call into the editor stalls. 4. The session worker reaches task.get() and waits without a deadline. 5. The user waits for handoff until the editor call returns.

dimensions.name: Resource lifecycle
dimensions.justification: WarmHoldOwner has a 30-second expiry, route-change exits, and explicit teardown. ASR recognizer release is correctly serialized after admitted work, but a native operation that never returns prevents its queued release from running. Without a process-level ASR deadline, this can retain the model and leave the session open. Actual native stall behavior needs device fault injection.

best_example.why_exemplary: The decided earbud hold has a fixed expiry and closes when routing or the device changes.

worst_violation.rule_violated: .claude/rules/architecture-rules.md RULE: no-idle-cost; named principle: bounded ownership of native resources
worst_violation.confidence_rationale: A queued release cannot run while the same single worker is stuck. The probability of a native stall on the founder's phone is unmeasured.
worst_violation.counterfactual: A stuck native load or decode can retain the ASR process and recognizer resources after the service is asked to close.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: The only release task sits behind the work that is not returning.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Block the recognizer's load or decode, close the service, and show that the ASR process and native allocation terminate within a fixed bound.
worst_violation.concurrency_interleaving: 1. The ASR worker begins native load or decode. 2. That call remains blocked. 3. Service destruction calls close from the main thread. 4. close enqueues free on the same single worker and returns. 5. The blocked task never finishes, so free never executes.

dimensions.name: Security and privacy
dimensions.justification: The sampled network path sends text only for selected cloud polish; provider keys use Android Keystore. PostHog string values require a declared key rule, Sentry exception messages are cleared, and the GenieX log callback discards vendor diagnostics. Model descriptors carry pinned revisions, byte counts, and hashes. These are strong static controls, but only a captured device network and crash payload can validate the final boundary.

best_example.snippet:
event.fingerprints = event.fingerprints?.filter { it in SentrySchema.fingerprints }?.ifEmpty { null }
        event.exceptions?.forEach { exception ->
            // Exception MESSAGES are always dropped, approved types included (G2 D7); the type and the
            // frames are what group and diagnose.
            exception.value = null
            exception.type = exception.type?.let(SentrySchema::exceptionType)
            exception.module = exception.module?.let(SentrySchema::module)
            exception.setUnknown(null)
            exception.mechanism?.let { mechanism ->
                mechanism.type = mechanism.type?.let(SentrySchema::identifier)
                mechanism.description = null
                mechanism.helpLink = null
                mechanism.meta = null
                mechanism.data = null
                mechanism.setUnknown(null)
            }
            sanitizeStack(exception.stacktrace)
best_example.why_exemplary: Sentry drops exception prose and unrecognized data before a crash event leaves the device.

refactor_targets.title: Give each ASR request a terminal deadline
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Add a per-take ASR deadline to DictationSessionCoordinator when transcribeFileForTake is issued. Disarm it on the first typed result or failure. On expiry, claim the take through TakeArbiter, record a typed ASR timeout reason, delete the captured file, show one failure notice, and ignore any late callback by take id. Add a rig row that holds a live ASR request without answering.

refactor_targets.title: End a stuck ASR process after its deadline
refactor_targets.rule_violated: Named principle: bounded ownership of native resources
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Add a process-level ASR watchdog keyed to the active load or decode. On expiry, mark the recognizer unavailable and terminate only the :asr process; let the main-process ASR deadline own the user outcome. Keep normal release serialized on the recognizer worker. Test a blocked native-operation seam and confirm process termination is bounded.

refactor_targets.title: Move captured-file cleanup out of the session owner
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Move the File existence, deletion, and failure reporting in DictationSessionCoordinator.deleteCapturedAudio into CapturedAudioCleanup. Expose one narrow delete(path) operation to the coordinator and use it from every current terminal callback. Remove the coordinator's direct java.io.File dependency.

refactor_targets.title: Separate insertion outcome recording from editor actions
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Extract AccessibilityInsertionRunner.finalizeInsertion, telemetry emission, and queued History update into an InsertionOutcomeRecorder in paste/. Leave request timing and editor action decisions in AccessibilityInsertionRunner, and pass it one immutable terminal outcome with take id, target, route, clipboard result, and elapsed time. Keep the existing first-wins repository operation.

refactor_targets.title: Split overlay gestures from view construction
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Move onTouch, onGesture, and cancelGesture into a BubbleGestureController fed by MotionEvent and returning commands. Move buildRoot, buildBubble, buildPill, and actionButton into a BubbleViewFactory. Keep RecordingAccessibilityOverlay as the window owner that applies those commands and mounts the views.

refactor_targets.title: Isolate legacy capture Binder adapters
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Move the large IAudioCaptureService.Stub implementation and the five-method IAudioTakeService.Stub construction from AudioCaptureService into CaptureBinderAdapters in audio/. Give the adapters narrow service operations and ListenerSlots. Keep every existing AIDL transaction and its legacy semantics unchanged.

refactor_targets.title: Make insertion admission return before editor work
refactor_targets.rule_violated: Named principle: bound external waits at an insertion boundary
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Change the accessibility handoff so its posted main-thread action only accepts and stores a PendingInsertion, then returns an accepted token. Schedule the first editor attempt as separate main-loop work; its verified or fallback outcome remains owned and announced by AccessibilityInsertionRunner. Remove the untimed FutureTask.get path only after a race test proves that timeout and acceptance cannot both claim one insertion.

phased_roadmap.title: Close the heart-path gap
phased_roadmap.rationale: An ASR request that never answers can hold the user's words path indefinitely. This change has no prerequisite.

phased_roadmap.title: Bound native cleanup and narrow central owners
phased_roadmap.rationale: The ASR process bound follows the new user-facing deadline. The cleanup and insertion extractions are independent and make later changes easier to review.

phased_roadmap.title: Reduce UI and Binder maintenance cost
phased_roadmap.rationale: The overlay and capture adapter moves are structural. The insertion admission change follows the outcome-owner extraction and needs a device race test.

least_confident_finding.why_low_confidence: The wait is an intentional fix for a proven double-outcome race. Static reading establishes a possible stall, but not that supported editors hold the main-thread action long enough to matter.
least_confident_finding.what_would_resolve_it: A delayed-editor instrumented run that records the main-looper action duration, owner handoff duration, and the final editor text.

top_not_assessed_gap.gap: End-to-end behavior when the :asr process stays alive but native load or decode stops returning
top_not_assessed_gap.runtime_test_required: On the S26 Ultra, hold native ASR load and decode independently without killing :asr; verify the recorder leaves Processing, one declared error reaches the user, the audio file is handled, and the ASR process is released within fixed bounds.
top_not_assessed_gap.why_this_matters_for_heart_limbs: ASR is part of the heart. A polish fallback cannot give the customer words when ASR never answers, so the owner must terminate the wait visibly.
